original_card.question: Can a decoder deliver the local paid mass in fewer, larger-rank children (block frame climbs instead of rank-1 to rank-3 steps)?
methods: Find one exact small decoding identity whose frame path climbs in blocks, and price its complete per-call profile.
Bound the best effective child rank achievable for one fixed support alphabet, including copies, frames and restoration.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A per-call local profile, with all copied information, frames and restoration counted, whose ceiling exceeds the selected word's by at least 5%; masked or overcomplete supports must change an assumption of the eight-term all-pairs bound.

first_step.inspect: Read the selected word's per-call local profile, its packing ceiling and the lever table; run levers.py for the ideal budget of the lever you target.
first_step.scope: Positive control and planning budget only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Before any synthesis, write the candidate per-call local profile (and centre charge / unpaid coordinates if changed) and screen it with ceiling.ceiling(); reject it if even the ideal ceiling does not beat the selected word's by your stated margin. Ideal budget: rank-16 delivery is 2.31x (levers.py).
original_card.bottleneck_link: Rank-1 children are about half of recursive cost; the selected word's effective child rank is about 3.9. Larger-rank delivery lowers recursive cost per unit of paid mass.
allowed_variations: One masked, overcomplete or block decoder family with exact labels and supports.
A scoped lower bound on effective rank for one alphabet.
If the coverage law, template or guard changes, derive an applicable fully charged replacement bound instead of applying the incumbent ceiling outside its scope.
scope_change_triggers: Repacking idle remainders of an unchanged word (covered by the packing ceiling).
Repeating the eight-term all-pairs search inside its proved scope.

actual_scope: Prove a sharp pairing-charge lower bound for every binary decomposition of the fixed orthogonal-frame decoder with at most one extra total.
scope_change_reason: The user assigned seed22 to complex suppliers. A rank-ten frame decoder with eleven totals changes the minimal-factorization contract without duplicating the clean-support or general minrank searches.
bottleneck_link: The current Eisenstein supplier template needs abstract copy charge at most 31. The theorem proves charge at least 40 for every at-most-eleven-total decomposition of the fixed frame decoder, including non-clean cancellation. This closes one complete mechanism before physical synthesis.
stop_rule: Stop after the universal argument, complete primary E8 proper-support census, independent coordinate and direct-factorization checks, negative controls, and overlap review.
evidence: PROOF.md proves the general q-frame theorem. verify.py checks 164110 proper-span supports, 159270 cosets, an independent 10700-generator traversal with all 164110 support ranks compared, 9200 exact complements, 5470 orthogonal complement pairs, and all decompositions with at most three active totals in a separate four-port model. Ten- and eleven-total E8 witnesses attain charge 40. These finite checks do not constitute a proof-assistant certificate or independent human review.
author: Charles Bethin, with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance
ai_assistance: Substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in the proof, implementation, verification, and writing. No external human review or proof-assistant validation.

open_questions.question: Can a different fitting matrix or at least twelve totals lower the full Eisenstein decoder charge below 32?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The fixed frame decoder with at most eleven totals cannot meet the inherited necessary cost gate.
open_questions.first_step: Price the complete optimistic invoice, then study two-dimensional extensions or a changed fitting matrix with exact pairing charges.
open_questions.blocked_by: No mathematical blocker established; the present theorem leaves this scope open.
